title: Add explicit 'Similarity-Mode' API header, runtime compatibility shim, and migration docs
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: Customers use both dot-product and cosine semantics for similarity in embeddings-based rerankers. Historically we normalized vectors at client-side in some SDKs and normalized in the service for other clients which led to inconsistent scores and surprising ordering when re-ranking. Several legacy clients assume raw dot-product and relied on downstream normalization; newer clients expect cosine. We need a deterministic server-side behavior that is explicit and backward-compatible.

Goal: Introduce an explicit API-level flag (Similarity-Mode header) that lets callers declare their expected scoring semantics (dot or cosine). Implement a runtime compatibility shim that preserves legacy behavior for unlabelled requests while encouraging explicit mode usage. Ship migration docs and SDK helpers so existing clients can opt into a consistent mode without regressions.

Scope: Service API, request router, runtime scoring layer, inference runtime tests, SDK updates (js/py), canary rollout, docs and deprecation policy. Not in scope: changes to index/retrieval pipelines outside the embeddings + rerank endpoint contract (handled by downstream infra teams in a separate ticket).
acceptance_criteria: API accepts an opt-in header 'Similarity-Mode: dot' or 'Similarity-Mode: cosine' and applies requested semantics to rerank responses
Requests without the header follow the existing legacy behavior (compatibility shim) with an audit log flag for telemetry
Unit and integration tests cover normalization permutations (client-normalized vs server-normalized) and ensure score stability within epsilon=1e-6
No latency regression > 5% at p50/p95 for rerank endpoints in canary; perf dashboard provided
SDKs (JS + Python) include helper methods and a migration guide; docs published with examples and recommended timeline
Canary rollout plan completed: 5% -> 20% -> 50% traffic with automatic rollback on error or >2% regression in rerank ordering vs baseline
Backward-compatibility plan documented with deprecation schedule and customer notification template
comments: 2025-02-20 - Asha Patel: Created ticket. Collected initial customer reports from Support (INC-8912) and tied to ENG-31321. Proposed header approach after small spike with PM and SDK leads.
2025-02-21 - Marco Ruiz: Implemented prototype in local runtime branch. Verified that adding explicit normalization in scoring layer resolves ordering differences for 3 canonical test prompts.
2025-02-22 - Emma Chen (PM): Reviewed trade-offs. Prefer header vs. new endpoint to keep surface area small. PM requests telemetry that distinguishes which mode produced the final score.
2025-02-23 - Nate Kim (Infra): Raised concern about routing and cache key changes. Suggested keeping cache key unchanged for legacy requests, adding mode into cache key for explicit-mode requests.
2025-02-24 - Marco Ruiz: Added integration tests and bench harness. Early canary scheduled once perf dashboard threshold validated. Drafted migration doc and SDK helper PRs for JS/py.
implementation_notes: API: Add optional HTTP header 'Similarity-Mode' with allowed values 'dot' or 'cosine'. Also accept query param 'similarity_mode' for legacy support via signed URLs.

Runtime shim: If header is absent, runtime inspects client agent and tenant config to choose one of: legacy-dot (legacy behavior), legacy-cosine (if tenant opted in), or default-cosine (new recommended). Record choice to audit log.

Scoring path: Implement a small scoring adaptor which, given scoring_mode and original embedding vectors, computes either raw dot or cosine (with robust L2 normalization that avoids divide-by-zero). Use fused kernels where available to minimize overhead.
Caching: For explicit-mode requests include 'similarity_mode' in cache keys. For header-less legacy requests keep previous cache key semantics to avoid invalidating cache for existing workloads.

Telemetry: Emit telemetry fields 'similarity_mode', 'server_normalized' (bool), and 'client_normalized' (bool). Add an event type 'similarity_mismatch' when both client and server normalization are present to help triage.

SDKs: Add EmbeddingsClient.score(embeddings, mode='auto'|'dot'|'cosine') helpers that set header and optionally perform client-side normalization. Default 'auto' sets header for new SDK versions to 'cosine'.

Tests: Create matrix tests: (a) client sends normalized vector + header 'dot' expected to still compute dot correctly, (b) client sends normalized vector + header 'cosine' no-op normalization, (c) unlabelled legacy requests reproduce previous scores within tolerance. Add fuzz tests for near-zero norms.

Canary: Start with internal tenants and low-traffic customers. Monitor rerank-order differences vs baseline using NDCG@10 on synthetic prompt set plus production validation set. Rollback triggers: ordering regression >2% or latency p95 increase >5%.
Docs & comms: Publish migration guide with examples for converting dot->cosine and verifying parity. Prepare customer notice for deprecation of implicit legacy behavior 6 months after GA.
Edge cases: Ensure deterministic tie-breaking when rounding causes equal scores; preserve previous tie-break order for legacy requests to avoid surprising churn.
